canonical_statement: The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of oral steroid therapy for restoring motor functions in patients with Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy (FCMD).
Eligibility required genetically diagnosed FCMD, age 3-10 years, clinically ascertained decline in motor function, and consent to steroid therapy.

population.label: Study-eligible FCMD patients
inclusion_criteria: Decline in motor function clinically ascertained
Consent to undergo steroid therapy provided by the patient or parent/guardian

canonical_statement: Nine patients were enrolled (4 boys, 5 girls): eight had a 3-kb homozygous FKTN insertion mutation and one had a composite heterozygous mutation; clinical forms were 1 mild, 7 typical, and 1 severe.

population.label: Enrolled FCMD cohort: 4 boys and 5 girls; 8 with 3-kb homozygous FKTN insertion and 1 with a composite heterozygous mutation; 1 mild, 7 typical, and 1 severe clinical form

canonical_statement: The study was an open-label, single-arm clinical study conducted at Tokyo Women's Medical University Hospital from February 2016 to March 2019.
Prednisolone was started orally at 0.5 mg/kg on an alternate-day basis; if ineffective after 1 month, the alternate-day dose was increased by 0.2-0.25 mg/kg each month up to 1.0 mg/kg.

exposures.details: Starting dose; escalation by 0.2-0.25 mg/kg alternate-day monthly after an inadequate 1-month response, maximum 1.0 mg/kg alternate-day.

canonical_statement: Motor function was evaluated with the GMFM, which comprises 88 items in five dimensions; dimension percent scores are calculated from item scores and the total score is the average of the five dimension scores.

outcome.definition: Gross Motor Function Measure (GMFM): 88 items across lying/rolling, sitting, crawling/kneeling, standing, and walking/running/jumping; dimension percent scores are calculated from item scores and the total score is the average of the five dimensions.

canonical_statement: The post-therapy GMFM evaluation was performed 6 months after drug compliance was confirmed.
Before-versus-after motor function was analyzed with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test in SPSS 27 using a significance threshold of P <= 0.05.
The mean change in GMFM total score after steroid therapy was +1.23 percentage points (SD 1.10), with P = 0.015 by Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: The mean GMFM difference between before and after the steroid therapy was +1.23 (SD, 1.10), and a P value of 0.015 represented significant improvement in GMFM.

canonical_statement: The authors identified the small sample size, different steroid doses among patients, and the long time required to confirm drug compliance as study limitations.
No statistical analysis of dose-response correlation was performed because of the small sample size.
The study did not establish long-term safety or long-term functional effects of steroid therapy, particularly when treatment is initiated at an early age.
The authors concluded that steroid therapy may contribute to short-term improvement or maintenance of motor function in patients with FCMD whose motor function has begun to regress.
The study datasets are available from the corresponding authors on reasonable request.
The study was funded by a psychological/neurological disease research grant (Grant 2-4) from the National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry, Japan, and supported by the SHISEIKAI Scientific Award.
The authors declared no competing interests.
